application_review: Conditioning the original finite mass has the exact intersection-event numerator and actual event denominator. A uniform positive lower bound on that denominator preserves every proved zero event limit, without requiring the conditioning event to tend to one.

For arbitrary finite exposure maps, the original pushforward coefficient equals the original fiber event mass. The average fiber-conditioned event probability under that pushforward is exactly the original event probability. Zero-mass fibers are handled explicitly using nonnegativity; no division by a presumed positive fiber is hidden.

The probability of exposure fibers whose conditional bad-event mass exceeds a fixed positive threshold is bounded by the original bad-event mass divided by that threshold and tends to zero whenever the original bad-event mass does.

The concrete short-exposure key records only earlier outside values, target-tail residues modulo M*W^w, target-tail binary dyadic bins, the pivot residue modulo M and the product short bin of width t_lo*R. Equal keys imply the retained earlier-variable exposure relation, equal dyadic bins and lower products, equal pivot residues and equal short-bin indices with one common width. Positive values lie in the asserted binary dyadic intervals.

The original raw array-stability failure limit survives any prior event with a fixed positive probability lower bound. Under its genuine conditioned short-exposure distribution, the probability of fibers with non-negligible conditional array-stability failure tends to zero. This is convergence in probability over fibers, not a claim that every fiber is good.
Reviewed conditioning denominator: the lower probability bound is explicit and positive. No transfer through arbitrary rare events is claimed.

Reviewed exact exposure averaging: the exposure law is the pushforward of the actual mass, and each posterior is normalized by its own actual fiber mass. Zero-mass fibers contribute zero by a proved intersection bound.

Reviewed concrete exposure: later coordinates and the exact pivot microcell are not recorded. Binary dyadic intervals, their common lower-product scale, full tail residue modulus and the product-bin width match the paper exposure.

Reviewed probability quantifiers: every fixed positive posterior failure threshold has a vanishing bad-fiber probability. The proof does not assert a uniform bound on every individual fiber, and does not infer marginal face invariance from interval stability.

Reviewed remaining scope: full cutoff-clipped exposure geometry, uniform bounded-multiple-box estimates, model-reading calibration, polynomial dependence, actual prior-good-event lower bounds and nilpotent recurrence still need their remaining connections. The main monochromatic theorem remains incomplete.

All named declarations are strictly elaborated and checked for transitive axioms. Prior proof sources and prior axiom sets remain unchanged. No independent kernel replay or full-target proof is claimed.

Integer realization now proves the actual master pair scale relation, exact natural numerator with its original rational value, canonical bounded full-modulus residues, all required divisibilities, uniform eventual fixed-integer divisibility, finite numerical slot bounds and the numerical own-target array-letter identity. The actual earlier-variable exposure fixes every residue and slot shift, full own-target numerators and array residues; exact affine tail dependence of each progression and the whole own-target progression sum is proved. Concrete integer-input polynomial array groups, their common nilpotence bound, input translations, pointwise lattice coset evaluation and exact affine model linear orbits are constructed. The genuine original native Lie polynomial-array coefficient algebra, bracket closure, high-degree cutoff and finite dimension are now proved; literal Lie evaluation homomorphisms and their lower-central compatibility are constructed. The same-step lower-central cutoff of the genuine array Lie algebra, injectivity of all integer evaluations and simultaneous coefficient recovery by one fixed finite integer evaluation set are now proved, including for the original native model. The actual binary product native Lie algebra, componentwise original exponential and global logarithm, and integration and inherited topology of every product Lie subalgebra are now proved. The complete native array coefficient algebra now embeds by one fixed finite family of integer inputs into the native Lie algebra of an actual finite original-group product. Its finite evaluation image integrates to a closed contractible simply connected subgroup, uniquely parameterized by coefficient exponentials. All-integer multiplication compatibility, the exact full exponential array subgroup, its group isomorphism and inherited-topology homeomorphism with the finite image, contractibility, simply connectedness, and discreteness of its pointwise Gamma-valued subgroup for discrete Gamma are now proved. Cocompactness of the exact all-integer pointwise lattice is now proved by actual lattice monomial spanning, rational-log intersection, positive-root character descent and continuous quotient transfer. The actual integrated subalgebra and full native array group now have constructed smooth manifold and Lie group structures on their inherited topologies, and all literal integer evaluations are smooth. The actual array group and exact lattice instantiate the existing NativeNilmanifoldData interface at the same original nilpotency step, with constructed compatible quotient metric. Integer input translations now preserve the actual graded coefficient Lie algebra, the full native exponential array group and its exact all-integer lattice; actual group and coset homeomorphisms and continuous coset evaluation with exact translation compatibility are proved. Array input translations are now proved smooth with smooth inverses in the existing original exponential charts. Original affine power-times-basepoint model arrays are proved to belong to the actual native array group; their exact evaluations, input translations and linear time orbit are proved both in the group and in its exact lattice coset space. Actual original and array discrete-lattice quotient manifolds are now constructed on the retained coset topologies; original quotient projections, all integer-input quotient evaluations and original quotient translations are smooth, with the latter having proved smooth inverses. The dependent product joint group, its exact product lattice, compact coset space, common nilpotency cutoff, original joint model orbit, component evaluations and input shifts are now constructed with exact formulas. The finite joint group now has its constructed finite-dimensional complete Lie model, global product exponential diffeomorphism and original smooth group operations, and instantiates NativeNilmanifoldData with the exact joint group, exact lattice and same common step. The original joint quotient is a smooth manifold with smooth component integer evaluations and smooth input-shift diffeomorphisms. Uniform quantitative smooth-observable bounds and model-reading calibration remain unproved. The finite short-bin pivot likelihood estimate and factor-three posterior domination relative to the original tail prior are now proved for the actual raw harmonic pivot law, with explicit full-cutoff containment, positive normalizer, unit residue and small-discretization hypotheses. The original dyadic-conditioned tail law is now proved equal to conditioning the original product law, and is dominated by 2^card(T) times product uniform. The actual short-bin posterior is now dominated by 3*2^card(T) times product uniform on prescribed dyadic residue bins, with explicit endpoint inequalities ensuring every pivot preimage lies in the cutoff. The original raw pivot probability of discarding short bins whose full preimages leave the buffered cutoff now has a uniform explicit bound and is proved to tend to zero for the actual master cutoffs and primorial roughness moduli. The proof covers any width bounded by the pivot gap, including modulus-aligned integer square-root widths, and any positive dyadic lower product. Actual product H-boundary probabilities now have a periodic cardinality estimate and exact original harmonic formula, without assuming coprimality of the tail product and H. Their averaged original joint probability tends to zero at actual master scales for margins bounded by a fixed multiple of K times the aligned integer square-root width, with K bounded by the auxiliary scale. The required square-root product-margin limit is proved from master growth. The literal numerical array arguments have a proved same-H-interval theorem under explicit whole-cell, slot and progression margins. The complete earlier-variable exposure disintegration, transfer through all prior good conditioning, treatment of cutoff-clipped dyadic bins, transfer of the now-proved original-raw simultaneous array stability probability through the remaining exposure and good conditioning, and eventual satisfaction of the remaining scale inequalities are still to be connected. The exact real-floor microcell identification, all-power growth of both actual width and progression length, eventual width positivity, and uniform prescribed finite-slot bounds over every modulus-square-bounded residue family are now proved. Uniform polynomial bounds for the literal numerator and scaled array progression, their finite-table epsilon-width estimates, and deterministic whole-microcell interval stability with margin 3*aux*width are now proved. Exact pivot disintegration for original global raw event masses, the actual outside-law support geometry, simultaneous finite-target boundary probability decay, and probability-one-limit whole-microcell array stability under the original raw law are now proved. Exact finite exposure event disintegration, positive-event conditioning transfer and bad-fiber probability decay are now proved. A concrete short-exposure key records the original outside values, tail residues and binary dyadics, pivot residue and t_lo*R product bin, with proved coordinate and bin identities. Raw array stability transfers to the resulting conditioned exposure distribution in probability when the actual prior event has a fixed positive mass lower bound. Full exposure support geometry, bounded-multiple-box uniformity and the required prior-event lower bounds remain to be assembled. HasAlignmentMonomialRecurrence remains an explicit unproved input. Its genuine nilpotent recurrence proof, the connection of the constructed joint model to all prescribed quantitative readings, microcell boundary and point-law estimates, and positive-probability Alignment bounds remain unproved.
